title: RFC 2692 -- SPKI requirements: certificate and validity instruments (DERIVED -- not verbatim)
$comment: DERIVED -- not verbatim. RFC 2692 contains NO formal grammar of any kind -- no ASN.1, ABNF, CDDL, JSON Schema or BNF, not even an informal template -- and it rules ASN.1 out: 'In particular, ASN.1 is not to be used.' (Implementation of Certificates, para 4, p.5). Every keyword in this file was written for this library record and must never be quoted as RFC 2692's own schema. Every member name is the library's, not the source's (the source names no fields), except 'delegation-allowed', which echoes a phrase the source quotes. ||| DERIVED FROM: RFC 2692, 'SPKI Requirements', C. Ellison, September 1999, Experimental, <https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2692.txt>, source sha256 6a88c1563590e8094bb37cda5c5d29ef70f8384e5a3a0528bce29c501826976d (.cache/rfc-2692.txt). Sections used: Abstract, Background, General Requirements, Validity and CRLs, Implementation of Certificates, List of Certificate Uses. ||| WHAT IT MODELS: the structures RFC 2692 says an SPKI certificate and its validity instruments must or should be able to carry, as JSON -- a certificate, a CRL, a positive revalidation instrument, and five certificate profiles drawn from the use list. Leaves the source names but never shapes (key, hash, name, date, signature, location, certificate identifier, authorization) are opaque. ||| TRACEABILITY: every $defs entry and every property carries x-status ('derived' = encodes a stated requirement; 'opaque' = named, no form given; 'tentative' = floated by the source with 'Maybe'), x-inferred (boolean) with x-inferred-reason when anything in it is not literally stated, x-quotes (locator, source line range, verbatim text) and a description that repeats the quotes. Quotes are one contiguous run of source characters with RFC line-wrapping undone (a line break and the next indent become one space; 'collision-' + 'free' joins with no space); in-line double spaces are kept; no quote crosses a page break -- a sentence that does is quoted in two parts. Locators use the section title (sections are unnumbered), paragraph or list item, and page. ||| WHAT NO KEYWORD HERE CAN CHECK -- date order, non-overlap across a CRL sequence, signature over the transmitted bytes, LR(0), no recursion, self-signature, distribution -- is in $defs/NOT-EXPRESSIBLE (x-constraints RC-01..RC-21, x-gaps G-01..G-15). Read it before trusting a green result. ||| ROOT: certificate. Validate a CRL, a revalidation instrument or a profile by reference, e.g. {"$ref": "spki-requirements.derived.schema.json#/$defs/crl"}. ||| constrained_by on each NOT-EXPRESSIBLE item lists the rfc-2692#R-NNNN requirements it renders or bears on, wired by the pass-3 cross-check against requirements.yaml; RC-04 and G-10 have none, and say why in constrained_by_reason. README.md maps every member here to its messages.yaml field. ||| NOT RECURSIVE: no $ref cycle exists in this file (checked), in keeping with the source's 'without any recursion'.

key-equivalence-certificate.description: INFERRED (see x-inferred-reason). Profile: a certificate by which a long-term ('certifying') key makes a short-term ('signed') key equivalent to itself, for listed purposes, until the certificate expires -- so a slow smart card is used only at login. The same item notes that this works against attempts to prevent delegation, which is where the tentative delegation-allowed bit comes from. NOT-EXPRESSIBLE.description: Collected findings, not a schema: never referenced, and 'not': {} makes it match nothing. x-constraints (RC-nn) are rules RFC 2692 states (or that this library infers, marked status 'inferred') which no JSON Schema 2020-12 keyword can check -- cross-member order, cross-instance relations, wire-encoding properties, distribution and judgement. Where a rule can be written as code it has a 'check' in pseudo-code over the JSON rendering; date_le/date_lt assume dates are totally ordered (inferred) and same_key(a, b) is true when two key identifiers denote the same key, so a key and the hash of that key are the same key (R-0061 allows a direct certificate's subject to be either). Not here: a verifier's decision at check time -- whether a certificate is accepted at a given time inside its validity period, or rejected because the current CRL it names lists it -- is a lifecycle, not a property of an instance, and is modelled in state-machine.yaml (M02, M03, M11, M14). x-gaps (G-nn) are places the source is silent where a schema needs an answer. Every item carries its verbatim basis. constrained_by lists the rfc-2692#R-NNNN requirements each item renders or bears on (wired in the pass-3 cross-check); an empty list carries a constrained_by_reason.
